History: Cai Lun Through the Fourdrinier Machine

sections.text:
```
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|              PAPERMAKING TIMELINE                                |
|                                                                  |
|  105 CE    Cai Lun → China        Invented / systematized        |
|  400s      Spread across East Asia Buddhist sutras, Tang culture |
|  700s      Arab world              Battle of Talas (751) → Islam |
|  1000s     Persia, North Africa    Samarkand, Baghdad            |
|  1100–1200 European contact        Fabriano, Italy (1276)        |
|  1400s     Gutenberg               Paper demand explosion        |
|  1700s     Industrial demand       Rag shortage crisis           |
|  1798      Robert's wire machine   First continuous machine      |
|  1807      Fourdrinier (London)    Commercial Fourdrinier        |
|  1840s     Wood pulp               Mechanical then chemical      |
|  1884      Dahl's kraft process    Dominant to this day          |
|  1900–1950 Machine scale-up        Speed, width, automation      |
|  1950–2000 Coatings, fillers       Graphic paper peak            |
|  2000–now  Digital disruption      Packaging growth              |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
